Pattern-write, window and key-layer idioms follow VECTOR and Analog BD (repeat98) and Sam Banks' MIT octabam editor tooling; firmware addresses cited from octabam and Play Modes (devilfish707).

presentation.label: EUCLIDEAN TRIGS
presentation.summary: Analog Rytm-style Euclidean sequencer: two pulse generators, rotations and a logic operator write real trigs on an audio track.
presentation.overview: Euclid Seq adds an EUCLID trig mode and turns an audio track's trigs into a Euclidean rhythm, as the Analog Rytm's Euclidean mode does. Two generators (PL1, PL2) spread their pulses evenly over the track's length; RO1 and RO2 rotate each, OP combines them (OR, XOR, AND, SUB) and TRO rotates the result. The module writes ordinary trigs into the pattern, so the stock sequencer plays them with its own tempo, track speed, swing, locks and conditions; it keeps no clock. While EUC is on, the TRIG keys cannot add or remove trigs on that track; holding a trig still edits its parameter locks.
highlights: PL1/PL2 pulses, RO1/RO2/TRO rotations and OR/XOR/AND/SUB, per track and pattern
Writes real trigs: stock playback, swing, locks, conditions and bank save
An EUCLID trig mode with its own main-screen panel; FUNC+RIGHT opens the six-dial EUCLID page
Follows PATTERN SCALE length changes; no clock of its own
usage: Hold FUNC and press DOWN until TRIG MODE shows EUCLID (audio tracks). The main screen shows the EUCLID panel.
Press FUNC+RIGHT to open the EUCLID page and YES to turn EUC on. A sets PL1, B PL2, D RO1, E RO2, F TRO and LEVEL the operator; C shows the track length.
Press NO to close the page. The page also opens with RIGHT on TRACK TRIG EDIT's TRIGS row. Press YES on the page again to turn EUC off; the trigs remain as ordinary trigs.

limitations: Deliberate stock-flow changes: TRIG MODE gets a seventh row, EUCLID, on audio tracks; in that mode FUNC+RIGHT opens the EUCLID page instead of shifting trigs in grid recording; RIGHT on TRACK TRIG EDIT's TRIGS row opens the page; with EUC on, the TRIG keys and live recording do not place or remove trigs on that track; on MKII in grid recording the trig keys show those trigs purple.
EUC settings and the EUCLID trig mode are runtime state: a reboot or project reload turns EUC off, forgets PL/RO/OP and returns to TRACKS; the generated trigs are ordinary pattern data and stay.
Purple trigs need the MKII panel; MKI trig LEDs stay stock.
Audio tracks only; MIDI tracks are not supported.
One functional MKII report on an earlier image; the EUCLID trig mode is emulator-tested only; worst-case chip timing is unmeasured.
Like every DRAM module, the build gives up about 10 MB of sample memory to the platform reserve.

storage.label: DRAM data
storage.conditions: One 16,384-byte settings table for 16 banks x 16 patterns x 8 tracks plus the unit's code, in the platform reserve. Exact totals not yet recorded.

processing.label: ColdFire processing
processing.conditions: Runs only on key and knob events on the UI task, never per step or per sample. Not yet measured.

impact.conditions: Knob turns on the EUCLID page with EUC on: one 64-step regeneration per event.

cpu.rationale: Work happens only on key, knob and length-change events: one pass over at most 64 steps. Nothing runs per step or per sample.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code, tables or buffers; stock DSP processing is unchanged.

memory.rationale: A 16 KB settings table and a few KB of code in the shared platform reserve; no per-instance copies.

tests.summary: Host gate: the generator matches an independent formulation on 633,984 settings. Emulator: 32 scripted checks pass on MKII and MKI panels (page, EUC, blocking, locks, length follow, playback timing, the EUCLID trig mode and FUNC+RIGHT). One functional MKII report on an earlier image.

license.declaration: Original code, icon and thumbnail by bretth18, MIT. Firmware addresses are cited from public module sources and read from the author's own OS; stock key handlers, strings and icon records are referenced by address, never copied. No Elektron firmware, extracted routines, tables or images are included.

access.location: Audio track: FUNC+UP/DOWN (TRIG MODE) chooses EUCLID; FUNC+RIGHT then opens the EUCLID page. Also RIGHT on TRACK TRIG EDIT's TRIGS row.
steps: Include Euclid Seq in your build and select an audio track.
Hold FUNC and press DOWN until TRIG MODE shows EUCLID; release FUNC.
Press FUNC+RIGHT to open the EUCLID page; press YES to turn EUC on.
Press NO to close the page. In grid recording, FUNC+BANK then RIGHT on the TRIGS row opens it too.
